starting_question: Why does NADH-driven ferredoxin/H2 production appear acetyl-CoA dependent despite an unfavorable redox step?

actual_observations.result: Crotonyl-CoA substitutes for the acetyl-CoA-generating system in lysates.
Purified complex reduces ferredoxin only with crotonyl-CoA; omission controls and NADPH substitution distinguish dependencies.
H2 assay gives 2.2 NADH and 1.4 crotonyl-CoA per H2; fully coupled 2:1:1 stoichiometry is an extrapolation.
Partial protein sequences identify the three locus tags. FAD/anoxia preserve activity; FMN does not substitute.

annotation_consequence: Coupled crotonyl-CoA and ferredoxin reduction by NADH, rather than an acetyl-CoA-activated standalone oxidoreductase. Do not equate artificial-acceptor dehydrogenase activity with physiological direction.
experiment_dependence: Purified-complex assays, hydrogenase-coupled gas chromatography, product mass spectrometry and subunit identification are decisive; not reproduced here.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors explicitly tested coupling against prior allostery. Detailed probe ordering and decision comparisons in traces are reconstructed.
verification_scope: Full relevant introduction, purification/assay methods, results, tables and discussion inspected; raw HTML and parsed paragraphs saved.

starting_question: Is NAD+-stimulated ferredoxin reduction allosteric control or part of a coupled transhydrogenation?

actual_observations.result: Recombinant NfnAB reduces ferredoxin with NADPH efficiently only with NAD+; NADP+ reduction by reduced ferredoxin depends on NADH.
Measured stoichiometry supports one two-electron ferredoxin plus NADH reducing two NADP+ in a reversible reaction.
Separated subunits largely lose coupled activity; reconstitution improves iron content and activity.

annotation_consequence: NADH-dependent reduced ferredoxin:NADP+ oxidoreductase with coupled reaction established. NADPH supply during fermentation is a physiological interpretation; artificial-acceptor or O2 activity does not establish its native role.
experiment_dependence: Paired donor/acceptor assays and stoichiometry; no native-gene phenotype establishing direction in this paper.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Coupling and proposed NADPH-supplying direction are authors' conclusions; retaining their different confidence levels is my synthesis.
verification_scope: Relevant expression/reconstitution/assay methods, results, stoichiometry figures and discussion inspected; supplements not independently reanalyzed.

starting_question: How can H2 supply low-potential ferredoxin for the initial methanogenic step without an extra membrane energy input?

actual_observations.result: Purified complex reduces ferredoxin almost completely with H2 only when heterodisulfide is supplied, beyond the uncoupled hydrogenase equilibrium.
Limiting-substrate experiments support approximately one two-electron ferredoxin per heterodisulfide; precise stoichiometry has stated analytical uncertainty.
Viologen contamination bypasses the apparent dependence through spontaneous electron transfer.

annotation_consequence: H2-dependent coupled ferredoxin/heterodisulfide reductase; the flavin mechanism and ATP-yield model have additional assumptions. Native ferredoxin potential was unknown; assays used clostridial ferredoxin.
experiment_dependence: Purified complex, equilibrium comparison and stoichiometry; high-phosphate in vitro assays and growth/H2-threshold measurements.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors report energetic argument, dye artifact and coupling evidence; I separate these from physiological stoichiometry assumptions.
verification_scope: Relevant entire primary body, methods, results, limitations and figure legends inspected. Supporting-information raw data not independently analyzed.

organism: Bacillus cereus ATCC10987, tested with Escherichia coli ACP/cells
starting_question: Which malonyl carrier can supply the methylated primer that allows fatty-acid chemistry to make a dicarboxylic biotin precursor?

actual_observations.result: B. cereus BioC complements E. coli delta-bioC.
8 mM malonyl-CoA gives only half the activity of 0.05 mM malonyl-ACP; other tested acyl-ACPs are inactive. Mass analysis supports methyl ester formation.
Active BioC overexpression blocks phospholipid labeling; SAM quality/product inhibition affect direct assays.

annotation_consequence: SAM-dependent malonyl-ACP carboxyl O-methyltransferase, masking the terminal carboxyl for pathway entry. Malonyl-CoA activity at high concentration is inadequate evidence for the physiological substrate.
experiment_dependence: Purified homolog, direct radiomethyl transfer/product analysis, complementation and labeling; cognate B. cereus ACP was not tested.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors report carrier correction and chemical rationale. Extension to other homologs requires evidence.
verification_scope: Full relevant primary introduction, methods, all results and discussion inspected; source figure numerical constants not independently fitted.

organism: Bacillus subtilis; complementation in Escherichia coli
starting_question: Does the assigned tRNA epoxide reduction require cofactors absent from inactive preparations?

actual_observations.result: Purified QueG lacking complete reconstitution is inactive on an oQ-containing RNA stem-loop. Iron/sulfide alone is insufficient; cobalamin addition restores activity.
Elemental/cofactor analysis supports two Fe-S clusters and one cobalamin; LC-MS measures oQ-to-Q conversion.
EPR supports base-off cobalamin without histidine replacement; cellular variants test essential residues.

annotation_consequence: Cobalamin/Fe-S-dependent epoxyqueuosine reductase. Inactive apo-protein does not falsify this function; dithionite/viologen assay donors do not identify the native electron-delivery system.
experiment_dependence: Cofactor reconstitution, RNA-product LC-MS, EPR and complementation are authors' experiments.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors distinguish cofactor occupancy from activity; native donor limitation is my bounded synthesis from assay composition.
verification_scope: Relevant purification, reconstitution, activity/complementation methods, cofactor results and EPR interpretation inspected; raw spectra not reprocessed.

organism: Pseudomonas aeruginosa; functional assay with Aspergillus niger Fdc1
starting_question: Why does a gene required for decarboxylation encode an FMN-binding protein without detectable decarboxylase activity?

actual_observations.result: DMAP binds UbiX; tested DMAPP/IPP do not yield comparable binding/modification evidence. Reduced FMN plus DMAP produces a prenylated flavin identified by mass/spectroscopy.
Protein-free reaction filtrate activates apo-Fdc1 after oxygen exposure; oxidized radical-form cofactor fails to activate.
Kinetic crystallography traps prenylation intermediates.

annotation_consequence: UbiX is a flavin prenyltransferase supplying the decarboxylase cofactor. The reconstitution assay assigns accessory chemistry; it does not establish the physiological DMAP source or universal precursor specificity.
experiment_dependence: Cofactor synthesis/reconstitution, filtration, MS/EPR and crystallography; no experiments reproduced here.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors' alternate-cofactor tests and mechanistic proposals are distinguished; assay scope includes a fungal partner, not direct bacterial native-substrate decarboxylation.
verification_scope: Relevant primary body and methods, including substrate tests, filtrate reconstitution and structure work, inspected.

starting_question: Which activated carbon precursor and reduction step can produce F420, and can a coupled assay assign the upstream enzyme's specificity?

actual_observations.result: 2019: PEP in FbiD/FbiA assays yields dehydro-F420; FbiB plus reduced-FMN regeneration yields mature reduced product. Broad archaeal extrapolation leaves an unexplained reductase.
2020: M. smegmatis lysate spiking favors PEP; deletion strains and LC-MS reveal dehydro-F420 only in delta-fbiB. FbiA copurifies with this product.

2022: changing only the downstream CofD/FbiA partner changes the apparent precursor preference. Cognate mycobacterial pairs favor PEP, Mycetohabitans pairs 3-PG, tested archaeal pairs 2-PL. GPPG is trapped structurally.

annotation_consequence: Annotate organism-specific coupled chemistry. Do not label every CofC homolog PEP-specific or require a hypothetical archaeal reductase from the 2019 generalization. Upstream promiscuity differs from pathway entry.
experiment_dependence: In-vitro reconstitution, native-cell metabolite/deletion evidence and cognate-partner comparisons are essential. Current record checks add no new physiology.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors report the revision and later partner correction; the two-route interrogation is reconstructed with known outcomes disclosed.
verification_scope: Relevant full primary results/discussion and assay/LC-MS/crystallography methods inspected in all three papers. No new flux measurements, crystallographic refinement or spectrum fitting.

starting_question: Where do hydroxyl oxygens come from when ubiquinone is synthesized without O2?

actual_observations.result: Anaerobic aro-pathway or pheA/tyrA defects lower ubiquinone; complementation/supplementation implicate prephenate downstream of the aromatic precursor requirement.
C4-18O-shikimate labels three ubiquinone oxygen positions; added unlabeled 4-hydroxybenzoate does not erase that pattern.
Authors remove O2-dependent hydroxylases to address trace oxygen and use an Fe-S ligand variant control.

annotation_consequence: Prephenate supplies oxygen in the UbiUV-associated pathway. Direct purified-protein hydroxylation, the electron acceptor and detailed oxidation mechanism remain unestablished in this paper.
experiment_dependence: Genetics, growth/complementation, lipid LC-MS and isotope synthesis/tracing; no direct in vitro UbiUV activity assay.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Oxygen-source conclusion is authors' experimentally supported inference; proposed electron-transfer mechanism is explicitly hypothetical.
verification_scope: Full relevant primary body, methods and figure legends inspected; supplement synthesis/raw isotopologue data not independently reanalyzed.

gene_protein: HemQ coproheme decarboxylase with HemY/HemH context
organism: Propionibacterium acnes, Mycobacterium tuberculosis; Staphylococcus aureus follow-up
starting_question: Can a chlorite-dismutase-like protein instead transform the iron-containing heme precursor, and what oxidant closes the reaction balance?

actual_observations.result: 2015 PNAS: purified pathway enzymes produce coproheme then protoheme; HemQ acts on Fe-coproporphyrin but not tested Ni-coproporphyrin. H2O2 or FMN supports product formation whereas several common acceptors do not.
2015 Biochemistry: time-resolved/HPLC/MS assays of S. aureus HemQ establish sequential oxidative decarboxylation; excess peroxide also destroys product heme.

annotation_consequence: Coproheme oxidative decarboxylase rather than chlorite dismutase or a coproporphyrinogen oxidase. Protein-bound heme can be substrate/product; an apparent heme cofactor is insufficient to assign chlorite chemistry.
experiment_dependence: Purified products, acceptor controls and follow-up kinetics. These assays alone do not identify the physiological oxidant supply in every organism.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors report pathway and oxidant alternatives; interpreting product loss as compatible with coupled destruction follows their controls.
verification_scope: Relevant primary body/results and main methods inspected for both; detailed supplementary purification protocols and later mechanistic revisions not checked.

starting_question: Does this membrane complex reduce the protein trisulfide intermediate rather than leave sulfide production assigned entirely to DsrAB?

actual_observations.result: Purified complex oxidizes menadiol when DsrC-trisulfide is supplied; omission controls and sequential substrate additions support dependency.
Thiol labeling/peptide MS detect reduced DsrC; derivatization/HPLC detects sulfide increasing with substrate. Recovery is only 40-50%, with quantitative limitations disclosed.
Strong chemical reductants fail to reduce trisulfide under tested conditions; its midpoint potential remains unknown.

annotation_consequence: Menadiol:DsrC-trisulfide oxidoreductase with sulfide product. Physiological quinol coupling is supported by analog/architecture, while proton translocation, DsrJOP role and thermodynamic potential remain unresolved.
experiment_dependence: Purified complex, product/thiol assays, peptide MS and quinol surrogate; neither membrane energization nor exact physiological stoichiometry directly demonstrated.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors distinguish binding, reaction and mechanistic proposals; kinetic versus thermodynamic barrier cannot be settled from failed chemical reduction alone.
verification_scope: Full relevant primary results, discussion, assay/product methods and limitations inspected; 2015 DsrAB source saw abstract only and is not counted as a separately verified case.

starting_question: Why does the purified hydrogenase accept neither NADH nor reduced ferredoxin alone at sufficient rates?

actual_observations.result: Combining NADH with enzymatically reduced native ferredoxin increases H2 formation; purified enzyme needs added FMN.
Limited-NADH experiments yield about 1.8 H2 per NADH, consistent with roughly equal electron input from both carriers.
Dithionite carryover short-circuits the dependence; pyruvate oxidoreductase can itself donate electrons, complicating ferredoxin kinetics.

annotation_consequence: Hydrogen production coupled to simultaneous NADH and reduced-ferredoxin oxidation, rather than either sole donor. Protein family and artificial-viologen activity alone miss the essential coupled donor requirement.
experiment_dependence: Native enzyme/POR/ferredoxin purification, donor omissions, gas chromatography and substrate-limited stoichiometry. Proposed internal bifurcation mechanism was not established by this work.
reasoning_reported_vs_reconstructed: Authors report assay revisions, donor synergy and proposed energetic interpretation. No unseen homolog is assigned solely from similarity here.
verification_scope: Full relevant primary methods, donor/stoichiometry results and discussion inspected; original raw gas-chromatography data not reprocessed.
